```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

prepDNAm turns Illumina DNA methylation array data into an analysis-ready beta
matrix and an HTML QC report. This guide covers installation, preparing a
run, running it (interactively or on a cluster), what it produces, and how to
export the results.

# Installation

prepDNAm needs R >= 4.1. Most dependencies come from Bioconductor, and some
of the optional ones from GitHub.

```{r}
install.packages(c("remotes", "BiocManager"))
BiocManager::install(c("minfi", "ChAMP", "impute"))
remotes::install_github("chiaraherzog/prepDNAm")
```

Install the manifest and annotation packages for the arrays you use:

| Array | `array =` | Packages |
|---|---|---|
| Infinium HumanMethylation450 | `"450k"` | `IlluminaHumanMethylation450kmanifest`, `IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19` |
| Infinium MethylationEPIC v1.0 | `"EPIC"` | `IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICmanifest`, `IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICanno.ilm10b4.hg19` |
| Infinium MethylationEPIC v2.0 | `"EPICv2"` | `IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICv2manifest`, `IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICv2anno.20a1.hg38` |
| Infinium Mouse Methylation | `"mouse"` | `chiaraherzog/IlluminaMouseMethylationmanifest`, `chiaraherzog/IlluminaMouseMethylationanno.12.v1.mm10` (GitHub) |

```{r}
# e.g. EPIC v2
BiocManager::install(c("IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICv2manifest",
                       "IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICv2anno.20a1.hg38"))
# mouse (GitHub)
remotes::install_github(c("chiaraherzog/IlluminaMouseMethylationmanifest",
                          "chiaraherzog/IlluminaMouseMethylationanno.12.v1.mm10"))
```

Optional packages add features; everything else works without them:

| Package | Source | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `ewastools` | `remotes::install_github("hhhh5/ewastools")` | SNP outlier metric, genotype agreement / sample identity checks |
| `rmarkdown`, `knitr`, `plotly`, `DT`, `htmltools` | CRAN | the HTML report |
| `EpiDISH` | Bioconductor | epithelial / fibroblast / immune cell fractions in the report |
| `WIDclocks` | `remotes::install_github("chiaraherzog/WIDclocks")` | epigenetic age in the report |
| `uwot` | CRAN | UMAP in the report |
| `readxl` | CRAN | `.xlsx` sample sheets |
| `shinyMethyl` | Bioconductor | `save_shiny = TRUE` |

`run_prepDNAm()` checks up front that the packages a configuration needs are
installed and says which are missing.

**pandoc.** The report needs pandoc (>= 2.0). RStudio, Positron and Quarto
include one. Outside those (e.g. plain `Rscript` or a cluster), install pandoc
or point R to an existing copy:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(RSTUDIO_PANDOC = "/Applications/quarto/bin/tools/aarch64")  # macOS, Quarto
```

# Preparing a run

## Input

`input` is one of:

- **IDAT files**: a directory, searched recursively (`.idat` or `.idat.gz`;
  each sample needs a `_Grn` and a `_Red` file). This is the full pipeline:
  control probes, Noob background and dye-bias correction, detection
  p-values, SNP probes, sex estimation.
- **A signal-intensity matrix** (e.g. a GEO supplementary file): one row per
  probe, columns `<sample> Unmethylated signal`, `<sample> Methylated signal`
  and optionally `<sample> Detection Pval`. Change the suffixes with
  `unmeth_pattern`, `meth_pattern`, `detp_pattern` if your file uses others.
- **A beta matrix** (`.csv`/`.txt` or `.rds`/`.Rdata`): probes in rows,
  samples in columns. With `normalise = "auto"` (default) BMIQ is only run if
  the type I / type II distributions look unnormalised.

The input type is detected automatically; set `input_type` to override.
Beta values must be between 0 and 1 (M-values are rejected).

## Sample sheet

The optional `pheno` sample sheet annotates the samples. Its `basename`
column must match the sample names in the data exactly. The standard columns
`sex`, `age` and `donor_id` switch on the sex check, the age comparison and
the genotype identity check in the report; see `vignette("sample-sheet")`.

## Configuration

All options go into one configuration object. The most common ones:

```{r}
library(prepDNAm)

cfg <- qc_config(
  input   = "data/idats",
  run_dir = "runs/study1",       # created by the run; its parent must exist
  array   = "EPICv2",
  pheno   = "data/samples.csv",
  exclude = "data/exclude.txt",  # optional: samples to drop from the start
  batch   = "chip",              # "none", "dir", "chip" or a sample sheet column
  cores   = 4,
  seed    = 1
)
cfg
```

- **Batches.** Reading and normalisation run per batch. Use `"dir"` for one
  subdirectory per plate, `"chip"` for the Sentrix ID, a sample sheet column,
  or `"none"`. By default: a `batch` column if the sample sheet has one, else
  `"dir"` if the IDAT directory has subdirectories, else `"none"`. Filtering,
  imputation and the sex call are always done on the pooled data, so the
  result is the same however you batch.
- **Thresholds.** Samples are removed if their median methylated or
  unmethylated log2 intensity is below `intensity_threshold` (9.5) or more
  than `failed_probe_threshold` (10%) of their probes have a detection
  p-value above `detp_threshold` (0.01). Probes are removed if they fail in
  more than `failed_sample_threshold` (10%) of samples, or are missing in
  more than `probe_na_threshold` (80%).
- **Probe lists.** chrY, SNP-overlapping, non-CpG and cross-reactive (Zhou et
  al. 2017) probes are removed by default (`remove_chrY`, `remove_snp`,
  `remove_non_cpg`, `remove_zhou`).
- **EPIC v2.** `compatible_subset = TRUE` (default for EPIC v2) also writes
  the matrix restricted to probes shared with EPIC v1, with v1 IDs, for
  combining with EPIC v1 data and for tools trained on EPIC v1.
- **Outputs.** `save_rs` (SNP probe betas, on by default where available),
  `save_sex`, `save_na_mask`, `save_shiny`, `export_csv` (see Exporting).

See `?qc_config` for every option.

# Running

```{r}
res <- run_prepDNAm(cfg)
res
```

This runs the stages in order:

1. `qc_init()`: creates the run directory, writes `config.yml`,
   `samples.csv` and `run_info.json`.
2. `qc_read()`: per batch, reads the data and extracts QC metrics.
3. `qc_filter_samples()`: per batch, flags samples to remove and why.
4. `qc_normalise()`: per batch, BMIQ on the retained samples.
5. `qc_merge()`: combines batches, removes probes, imputes, calls sex.
6. `export_beta_csv()`, if `export_csv = TRUE`.

The report is a separate step:

```{r}
qc_report("runs/study1", open = TRUE)
```

**Resuming.** Each stage skips work whose outputs already exist. If a run
stops (an error, a killed job), fix the cause and call
`run_prepDNAm("runs/study1")` again: it continues from where it stopped. A
failed stage leaves `FAILED_<stage>.txt` in the run directory with the error
and traceback. Use `force = TRUE` to recompute everything.

A run directory belongs to one configuration: calling `run_prepDNAm()` with
different options on an existing run directory is an error (use a new
`run_dir`, or `force = TRUE`). `export_csv` is the exception and can be
switched on for a finished run.

**Stages one at a time.** The stages can also be called individually, which
is useful for inspecting intermediate results or running batches in parallel
as separate jobs:

```{r}
qc_init(cfg)
qc_read("runs/study1", batch = "206467010001")
```

`run_summary("runs/study1")` shows sample and probe counts and the status and
duration of every stage.

## On a cluster

`inst/scripts/run_prepDNAm.R` runs a configuration from a YAML file whose
keys are the arguments of `qc_config()`:

```yaml
# study1.yml
input: /data/idats/study1
run_dir: /data/runs/study1
array: EPICv2
pheno: /data/pheno/study1.csv
batch: chip
cores: 8
export_csv: true
```

```sh
script=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts/run_prepDNAm.R", package = "prepDNAm"))')
Rscript "$script" --config study1.yml            # add --force, --quiet as needed
```

The exit status is non-zero if a stage failed. For example, with Slurm:

```sh
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=prepDNAm
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=8
#SBATCH --mem=64G
#SBATCH --time=12:00:00
module load R
script=$(Rscript -e 'cat(system.file("scripts/run_prepDNAm.R", package = "prepDNAm"))')
Rscript "$script" --config study1.yml --quiet
```

`cores` is capped at what the job was allocated. Resubmitting the same job
after a failure resumes the run. Memory use grows with the number of samples
per batch (read and normalisation) and with the total number of samples (the
merge step holds the pooled matrix).

# Outputs

Everything is written into the run directory:

| File | Content |
|---|---|
| `beta_merged.rds` | final beta matrix, probes x retained samples |
| `beta_merged_compatible.rds` | EPIC v2: EPIC v1/v2 compatible probes with v1 IDs |
| `pheno_postQC.rds` | sample sheet of the retained samples with QC metrics and predicted sex |
| `sample_qc.csv` | QC metrics of all samples, with `removed` and `reasons` |
| `probes_removed.csv` | removed probes and the reason |
| `imputed.csv` | per sample: number of values masked and imputed |
| `rs_merged.rds` | SNP probe betas of the retained samples |
| `config.yml`, `samples.csv`, `run_info.json`, `log.txt` | configuration, sample sheet, versions / seed / checksums / stage timings, log |
| `batches/<batch>/` | per-batch intermediate files |
| `report/` | the HTML report |
| `export/` | CSV exports |

```{r}
beta  <- readRDS("runs/study1/beta_merged.rds")
pheno <- readRDS("runs/study1/pheno_postQC.rds")
stopifnot(identical(colnames(beta), pheno$basename))
```

# The report

`qc_report()` writes one HTML page per topic into `run_dir/report/`; open
`index.html`. Each page is a single self-contained file that can be shared on
its own (`self_contained = FALSE` writes smaller pages that share a
`site_libs/` folder instead).

| Page | Content |
|---|---|
| Overview | run details, samples and probes retained, per-batch pass rates, removed samples |
| 1 Samples | every sample with all QC metrics and removal reasons (searchable, exportable) |
| 2 Controls | Illumina control probes (IDAT input) |
| 3 Intensities | median intensities and failed-probe fractions against the thresholds, signal-to-noise per sample |
| 4 Densities | beta distributions before and after normalisation, per sample |
| 5 Identity | predicted vs reported sex, genotype-based donor checks, immune cell fractions, epigenetic age, marker CpGs |
| 6 PCA / UMAP | dimensionality reduction and association of principal components with sample variables |
| 7 Run | configuration, thresholds, stage timings, package versions |

Pages show a short note instead of content that is not available for the
input type or array. The report can be re-rendered at any time without
recomputing (`force = TRUE`); `sex_col` and `donor_col` name sample sheet
columns that do not follow the standard names.

Every plot and table is made by an exported function (`qc_plot_*()`,
`qc_table_*()`, `qc_estimate_*()`, `qc_dimred()`), so the same figures can be
used in your own reports:

```{r}
rd <- qc_data("runs/study1")      # load once, reuse
qc_plot_intensities(rd)
plotly::ggplotly(qc_plot_densities(rd, "bmiq"))
qc_table_sex(rd)
```

To look at the SNP probes of each donor's samples against each other (one
page per donor):

```{r}
qc_snp_pairs_pdf("runs/study1")   # writes runs/study1/snp_pairs.pdf
```

# Exporting

`export_beta_csv()` writes the final beta matrix and sample metadata as CSV in
the DNA Methylation Array Data Standard (V-2410), the format read by
`biolearn`: a `cpgSite` column and one column per sample, betas rounded to
three decimals, `NaN` for missing values, at most 1000 samples per file; and
a metadata file with `SampleID`, `Sex` (0 = female, 1 = male), `Age`,
`PredictedSex` and the other sample sheet columns. Probe IDs are as in
`beta_merged.rds` (EPIC v2 IDs keep their suffix); the compatible export has
EPIC v1 IDs. Rounding to three decimals follows the standard; `digits = NULL`
(or `qc_config(export_digits = "full")`) keeps full precision.

```{r}
export_beta_csv("runs/study1")                              # into runs/study1/export/
export_beta_csv("runs/study1", sample_id = "geo_accession")  # use another ID column
export_beta_csv("runs/study1", compatible = TRUE)            # EPIC v2: v1-compatible matrix
export_beta_csv("runs/study1", digits = NULL)                # full precision, as beta_merged.rds
```

With `qc_config(export_csv = TRUE)` the export runs at the end of
`run_prepDNAm()` (for EPIC v2 both the full and the compatible matrix).
